strengths: Novel curriculum-based approach to learning procedural knowledge from declarative instructions; elegant connection to partial evaluation
Comprehensive experimental design across multiple domains (algorithms, grammars), model families (Qwen, Llama, GPT-4o), and model sizes with well-motivated ablations
Rigorously demonstrates core claim: single instruction can substitute for ~100 execution examples in controlled settings
Both proactive and retroactive curricula validated; explicit ablations show both stages are necessary for strong performance
Insightful analysis of reliability, bias correction, representation formats (code vs. NL), and limited compositional capability
Important safety implications for data curation and model behavior; clear commitment to reproducibility with promised open-sourced code and datasets
Clear problem formulation with well-defined losses and formal framework
weaknesses: Limited domain scope: primarily synthetic datasets (Random Arithmetic with basic operations, procedurally generated CFGs); real-world validation on LeetCode shows retroactive PBB performs comparably to baseline, undermining practical value

Modest absolute performance on unpaired instructions (~37% for Random Arithmetic); substantial gap between paired/unpaired performance raises questions about practical applicability versus in-context instruction following
Natural language instructions perform substantially worse than code; dismissal as 'scaling issue' is unconvincing; severely limits real-world applicability

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: paper invokes 'latent learning' without deeply explaining why train execution gradients activate test knowledge; limited probing of representations learned in each stage

Context augmentation shown to be 'important' (20 templates per dataset); sensitivity to augmentation quality/quantity underexplored; Appendix C suggests single-stage SFT approaches PBB performance with repetitions, indicating augmentation + repetition does substantial work

Baseline comparisons limited to Algorithm Distillation; no comparison to few-shot in-context learning or other curriculum/meta-learning approaches; proactive PBB's Stage 1 meta-training cost not fully accounted in sample efficiency claims
Limited compositional capability: only shown for two-function composition; performance degrades substantially without explicit chain-of-thought reasoning
Modest statistical rigor: some experiments have overlapping confidence intervals yet differences are claimed; unclear replication counts for some results; no formal significance testing
